title: Cap. VII close (open): punishment presupposes fault; negative reprobation denies unowed benefit
pass_a_gloss: That former will of punishing in God cannot or ought not to be considered, except with antecedent respect to the sin of the person to be punished, as a demeritorious cause; but this will of passing by, or nolition, so to speak, of predestinating, can be considered without antecedent respect to the sin of the non-elect person. But the reason of this discrimination is to be sought from this, that punishment is an act of vindicative justice, and therefore presupposes a fault worthy of vengeance: But non-election or negative reprobation is not a punishment, but the negation of a gratuitous benefit, which God is bound to exhibit to no one; and therefore by the nature of the thing it hardly presupposes an antecedent fault.
pass_b_english: The will to punish in God cannot be considered without prior regard to the sin of the one to be punished, as demeritorious cause. But the will to pass by — or nolition, so to speak, of predestinating — can be considered without prior regard to the non-elect person's sin. Why the difference? Punishment is an act of vindicative justice, and so presupposes a fault worthy of vengeance. Non-election or negative reprobation is not a punishment, but denial of a gratuitous benefit God owes no one — and so by its nature hardly requires an antecedent fault.
source_text: Prior illa voluntas puniendi in Deo considerari non potest aut debet, nisi cum respectu antecedaneo ad peccatum personae puniendae, tanquam causam demeritoriam; sed haec voluntas praetereundi, vel noluntas, ut ita loquar, praedestinandi, considerari potest absque respectu antecedaneo ad peccatum personae non-electae. Ratio autem hujus discriminis inde petenda est, quod punitio sit actus vindicativae justitiae, ac proinde culpam vindicta dignam praesupponit: Non-electio autem sive reprobatio negativa non poena sit, sed gratuiti beneficii negatio, quod Deus nemini tenetur exhibere; ac proinde ex natura rei culpam antecedaneam haud praerequirat.
